How can I share my screen during a kMeet call?
ground_truth: To share your screen in kMeet: 1) Have the desktop app (macOS/Windows) or mobile app (Android) - screen sharing is not yet available on iOS. 2) Create or join a meeting. 3) Click on the screen icon with an arrow to 'Share your screen'. 4) Validate authorization to access screen content. 5) Choose to share the entire screen or a specific window. 6) Click button to start sharing. 7) To stop, click the toolbar icon again. Note: Permissions may require a restart on first use.
key_points: choose entire screen or specific window
actual_response:
**How to share your screen during a kMeet call**

- **Prerequisites**  
  - You must use the **desktop app** (macOS / Windows / Linux) or the **Android** kMeet app.  
  - The **iOS** app does **not** support screen sharing.  
  - You need to be inside an active meeting (created or joined).  
  - The first time you share your screen, your operating system will ask for **screen‑recording / accessibility** permissions – you may need to restart the app after granting them.  
  - On macOS, go to **System Settings ▶ Privacy & Security ▶ Screen Recording** and add the browser you use (or the kMeet desktop app) to the list of allowed apps.  
  - On Android, enable the “Screen capture” permission for kMeet under **Settings ▶ Apps ▶ kMeet ▶ Permissions**.  
  - *Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2477/share-your-screen-on-kmeet*

- **Step‑by‑step to start sharing**  
  1. Open kMeet via **kmeet.infomaniak.com** or launch the desktop/Android app and **create** or **join** a meeting room.  
  2. In the toolbar, click the **screen‑share icon** (the icon with an arrow).  
  3. A warning may appear – read it and **authorize** the screen‑capture request (your OS may ask for permission).  
  4. By default the **entire screen** is shared. You can also choose a **specific window** (e.g., a single application) if you only want to show that window. *(Note: if you intend to let participants draw on the shared content, you must share the full screen.)*  
  5. Click the **“Start Sharing”** button to begin broadcasting.  
  6. To stop the broadcast, click the same toolbar icon again.  
  *Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2477/share-your-screen-on-kmeet*

- **Additional features & caveats**  
  - While sharing, participants can **draw** on the shared screen using the pencil icon in the toolbar (only available when the share originates from the **desktop app**).  
  - If you start sharing from the web version, participants will see a message prompting them to enable drawing; this step is not required for pure screen sharing.  
  - **Remote control** of the shared device is also possible, but it requires the same full‑screen share and the other user’s acceptance.  
  - If the screen‑share button remains greyed out, check your OS security settings (see the “Solving a problem on kMeet” guide).  
  - Screen sharing is **not available** on the iOS app; only desktop and Android clients support it.  
  *Sources: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2620/draw-on-kmeet, https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2622/remotely-control-a-device-with-kmeet, https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/289/solving-a-problem-on-kmeet*

actual_response:

  [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2397/create-a-kmeet-meeting-side-room]

- **Platform availability** – Side rooms are available on **all kMeet platforms** (Web, Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android). No platform‑specific limitation is mentioned in the documentation.  
  [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2397/create-a-kmeet-meeting-side-room]

  [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2397/create-a-kmeet-meeting-side-room]

  [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2397/create-a-kmeet-meeting-side-room]

- **Important notes / warnings** – Side rooms are **temporary**; they exist only during the meeting and are removed when the meeting ends. Participants can join or leave a side room at any time, and the moderator can **force a participant to join a side room**.  
  [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2397/create-a-kmeet-meeting-side-room]

  2. **Wait until participants have joined** the main meeting.  
  3. **Click the multi‑user icon** in the toolbar.  
  4. **Click the button to add a side room**.

question: How can I record a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To record a kMeet meeting: Prerequisites: Have a kDrive, be the moderator, and don't use encrypted meeting with custom key. Steps: 1) Start kMeet. 2) Once in the meeting, click on the action menu (three dots). 3) Click 'Start recording'. 4) Log in to Infomaniak if needed and select a kDrive for storage. 5) To stop, click the toolbar again and choose 'Stop recording'. 6) The recording is saved to the kDrive root in .mp4 format when all participants leave. Maximum duration is 3 hours.
actual_response:
**How to record a kMeet meeting**

- **Prerequisites**  
  - You must have a **kDrive** (standalone or included in a kSuite/my kSuite).  
  - You must be the **moderator** of the video conference.  
  - Do **not** use an encrypted conference with a custom key – recordings are not possible in that mode.  
  - The recording is saved as a **.mp4** file, with a maximum duration of **3 hours**.  
  - The recording is processed **server‑side**, so it does not increase the load on the device that started it.  
  - Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2472/save-a-kmeet-meeting-on-kdrive  

- **How to start a recording**  
  1. Open **kMeet** via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or through one of the desktop/mobile apps.  
  2. While in the meeting, click the **action menu (○○○)** in the kMeet toolbar.  
  3. Click the **record icon (◉ Start recording)**.  
  4. Confirm the action; if needed, log in to your Infomaniak account, select the target kDrive, and press the **Start** button.  
  5. The recording now runs in the background on the server.  
  6. To stop it, click the toolbar again and choose **Stop recording**, then confirm.  
  7. After stopping, you may be taken directly to the recording location in kDrive.  
  8. The video file appears **at the root of the selected kDrive** as soon as the virtual room is closed (i.e., when all participants have left).  
  9. Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2472/save-a-kmeet-meeting-on-kdrive  

- **Important notes / warnings**  
  - Only **moderators** can start or stop a recording; regular participants cannot.  
  - Recording is **not available** for meetings that are encrypted with a custom key.  
  - The recording stops automatically when the meeting ends; it will not continue after the last participant leaves.  
  - Because the recording is stored on kDrive, you can later manage, share, or download the .mp4 file just like any other file in your kDrive.  
  - The feature is available on the web client and on all desktop/mobile apps; there is no platform‑specific restriction mentioned.  
  - Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2472/save-a-kmeet-meeting-on-kdrive  

- **Related actions**  
  - After recording, you can **open, share, or move** the .mp4 file within kDrive.  
  - You can **stop** an ongoing recording at any time using the same toolbar button.  
  - Recordings can be **converted or archived** using standard kDrive functions, but the documentation does not specify additional conversion tools.  
  - Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2472/save-a-kmeet-meeting-on-kdrive  

---

**Summary** – To record a kMeet meeting, be a moderator with an existing kDrive, start the recording from the toolbar, confirm and select the target kDrive, stop it when finished, and the resulting .mp4 file will appear in the root of that kDrive once the meeting ends. All steps and requirements are detailed in the Infomaniak FAQ here: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2472/save-a-kmeet-meeting-on-kdrive.

question: How do I set a password for my kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To protect a kMeet meeting with a password: 1) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or app. 2) Start a new meeting. 3) Enter the meeting room name. 4) Click on 'security options'. 5) Enable the toggle switch to 'Protect access'. 6) Create the password. 7) Click Continue to start. 8) Share both the meeting link/code AND the password with participants. You can also enable end-to-end encryption from security options (works only with Chromium-based browsers).
actual_response:
**How to set a password for your kMeet meeting**

- **Prerequisites**
  - You must be creating a new kMeet meeting (via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or one of the kMeet apps).
  - No special account type is required; any user who can start a meeting can set a password.

- **Steps to protect the meeting with a password**
  1. Start kMeet and click **“Start a new meeting”**.  
  2. Enter a **name** for your meeting room.  
  3. Click the **security options** (the shield‑like icon).  
  4. Turn on the toggle **“Protect access.”**  
  5. **Create the password** you want participants to use.  
  6. Click **“Continue”** to start the meeting.  
  7. (Optional) Specify the name you’ll use as a participant.  
  8. **Share the meeting link or code + the password** with all participants.  
     - You can re‑display or review the password by using the dedicated **“Invite participants”** button before the meeting starts.

- **User role requirement**
  - No moderator or administrator role is needed just to set a password; any user who creates the meeting can enable protection.

- **Important notes / warnings**
  - The password must be shared with every participant; anyone without it cannot join.  
  - You can review or change the password via the invitation screen before the meeting begins.  
  - After setting the password, the meeting will not start until you click **Continue**; otherwise the room remains in a protected (waiting) state.  
  - If you later need to disable the password, you can return to the same security options and turn off **“Protect access.”**

- **Related actions you might also use**
  - Set an **encryption key** (same security options panel) for additional protection.  
  - Manage participants (approve/deny, remove, or make new moderators) once the meeting is in progress.  
  - Record the meeting on kDrive (requires moderator status and no custom encryption key).  

**Source:** Secure a kMeet meeting with a password and encryption key – [https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2464/secure-a-kmeet-meeting-with-a-password-and-encryption-key](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2464/secure-a-kmeet-meeting-with-a-password-and-encryption-key)

question: How can I livestream a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To livestream a kMeet meeting: Prerequisites: Must be a moderator (no Video Streaming offer required). Steps: 1) Start kMeet via ksuite.infomaniak.com/kmeet or app. 2) Once in the meeting, click the action menu (three dots). 3) Choose 'Start live broadcast'. 4) Click 'Start' button. 5) Wait for Video Streaming to be created. 6) Copy the stream URL and share it with viewers. 7) A symbol and audio alert indicate the broadcast start. The stream is continuous for max 24 hours and stops when the kMeet meeting ends.
actual_response:
**Prerequisites**  
- You must be a **moderator** of kMeet to create a live‑broadcast link (owning a Video Streaming offer is **not** required).  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)

**Platform limitations**  
- No specific platform restrictions are mentioned; the broadcast can be started from the web interface (**ksuite.infomaniak.com/kmeet**) or from the desktop and mobile apps (macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android).  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)

**Technical specifications**  
- The live stream can be broadcast **continuously for a maximum of 24 hours**; it disappears as soon as the kMeet meeting is stopped.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- The stream is delivered via a **unique URL** that can be copied and shared; viewers can open it in any web browser without logging in.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- Broadcasting via Video Streaming provides **higher broadcast resolution** and avoids vocal interruptions, making it suitable for large‑scale, passive events.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- A **symbol** and an **audible alert** indicate when the broadcast has started.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)

**User role requirements**  
- Only a **kMeet moderator** can initiate a Video Streaming broadcast.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)

**How to livestream a kMeet meeting**  
- Start kMeet via **https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kmeet** or launch one of the kMeet applications (desktop or mobile).  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- In the meeting toolbar, click the **action menu** represented by three dots (**○○○**).  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- Choose **“Start live broadcast”** from the menu.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- Click the **“Start”** button to begin the stream.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- Wait for the Video Streaming stream to be created; a link will appear in the same location.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- Click the **icon on the right** of the displayed link to **copy the URL**, then paste that URL into a message to share with participants.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- A **symbol** and an **audible alert** confirm that the broadcast is live.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  

**Important warnings / notes**  
- The stream **becomes inaccessible immediately** after the kMeet meeting is stopped; there is no automatic archive.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- Only the moderator can start the live broadcast; other participants cannot initiate it.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- Viewers (guests) do not need an Infomaniak account and have **read‑only access** to the stream.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)

**Related actions**  
- To **stop** the broadcast, click the same toolbar icon and select **“Stop”**.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- The copied stream URL can be shared in **kChat** or any other channel to invite additional viewers.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)  
- If you need to reuse the feature, you can create a new live‑broadcast link in a future kMeet meeting.  
  (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode)

question: How do I install kDrive on Linux?
ground_truth: To install kDrive on Linux: Prerequisites: Download the kDrive .AppImage file, install libfuse2 (required for Ubuntu 23.04+: sudo apt install libfuse2), D-Bus, and gnome-keyring or kwallet. Steps: 1) Place the .AppImage file in an 'Applications' folder. 2) Right-click the file and select 'Permissions'. 3) Check 'Allow executing file as a program'. Note: Officially supported on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS+ with GNOME or KDE. Lite Sync and right-click context menu not available on Linux. For Ubuntu startup, add to 'Startup Application Preferences'. For GNOME icon, install AppIndicator extension.
key_points: Lite Sync not available on Linux
actual_response:
**How to install kDrive on Linux**

- **Prerequisites**  
  - Download the kDrive desktop application for Linux (an `*.AppImage` file) – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  - Ensure **FUSE v2** is installed; on Ubuntu 23.04+ you must run `sudo apt install libfuse2` – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  - D‑Bus must be available (normally installed by default) – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  - **Gnome‑keyring** or **KWallet** are required (usually pre‑installed, but may be missing on lightweight distros) – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  - Official support is limited to **Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (and later) with GNOME or KDE** desktop environments; other distributions may work but are unsupported – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  

- **Technical specifications**  
  - The installation package is a **`.AppImage`** file – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  - The file must be marked as **executable** before it can be run – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  

- **Installation steps**  
  1. Place the downloaded `.AppImage` file in a folder (e.g., `Applications`) – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  2. Right‑click the file → **Properties** → **Permissions** → enable **“Allow executing file as a program”** – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  3. Double‑click the AppImage to start the installer; if nothing happens, verify that `libfuse2` is installed and the file is executable – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  4. (Optional) Add the AppImage to **Startup Application Preferences** so kDrive launches automatically at login – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  5. On GNOME, if the application icon does not appear, install the **AppIndicator** extension – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  

- **Important warnings / notes**  
  - On newer Ubuntu versions (23.04+) the default FUSE version is too recent; you must manually install `libfuse2` or the AppImage will not run – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  - **Lite Sync** and the **right‑click context menu** are **not available** on Linux – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2374/sync-kdrive-across-different-devices]  
  - The app is officially supported only on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS+ with GNOME or KDE; using it on other Linux flavors is at your own risk – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  - Some lightweight Linux distributions may lack Gnome‑keyring or KWallet, which are required for proper operation – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  

- **After installation**  
  - A kDrive folder is created at the location you selected; it synchronizes files with your kDrive account – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux]  
  - You can open the app’s preferences via the notification‑area icon (⋮) to configure sync settings, choose folders, etc. – [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2374/sync-kdrive-across-different-devices]

question: How can I share a file from kDrive?
ground_truth: To share a file/folder in kDrive: 1) Access kDrive web app at ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive. 2) Right-click on the file/folder. 3) Click 'Share...' at the top of the menu. Options: a) Activate a public share link (with options for modification, expiration date, password, download authorization). b) Or enter a kDrive user, contact email, or work team. For each person, define rights: 'viewing', 'modification', or 'management'. Recipients without Infomaniak account can create one free. Warning: deactivating/reactivating public link changes the URL.
key_points: recipients can create free Infomaniak account
actual_response:
- **Prerequisites**  
  - You must have an active kDrive account and be logged in to the service.  
  - You must be the owner of the file (or have edit rights) to share it.  
  - To manage sharing for folders inside **Organization Folders**, you typically need to be an Organization administrator or moderator.  
  - External recipients must possess an Infomaniak account (free or paid) to access a share.  
  - Sources: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2382/share-data-from-the-kdrive-web-app; https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1793/manage-the-sharing-of-the-organizations-kdrive-folders  

- **Platform limitations**  
  - Sharing is performed through the **kDrive web app** (https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive).  
  - The same actions can be carried out via the desktop client on macOS, Windows, and Linux, but the step‑by‑step instructions below refer to the web interface.  
  - Mobile apps do not provide full sharing options; they are limited to viewing shared content.  
  - Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2382/share-data-from-the-kdrive-web-app  

- **Technical specifications**  
  - Share links can be generated for **any file type**.  
  - For collaborative formats such as **.docx, .xlsx, .pptx**, you can enable online editing; other file types remain view‑only.  
  - Share links support optional **expiration dates**, **password protection**, and **download restrictions**.  
  - No specific size limit is mentioned in the documentation, implying standard kDrive storage limits apply.  
  - Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2382/share-data-from-the-kdrive-web-app; https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2399 (collaborative editing)  

- **User role requirements**  
  - Only the **file owner** (or a user with edit permissions) can initiate a share.  
  - Managing shares for **Organization Folders** may require **Organization administrator** privileges.  
  - Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1793/manage-the-sharing-of-the-organizations-kdrive-folders  

- **Important warnings or notes**  
  - Deactivating and reactivating a public share link **changes the URL** and invalidates the previous link.  
  - External users **must have an Infomaniak account**; public links are not accessible to completely anonymous users.  
  - Guests receiving a share link have **read‑only access** unless you explicitly enable editing for collaborative formats.  
  - Misconfiguring expiration or password may unintentionally lock out intended recipients.  
  - Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2382/share-data-from-the-kdrive-web-app; https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2859/understanding-kdrive-shares-web-desktop-app  

- **File types and extensions**  
  - Any file extension can be shared.  
  - Editing is supported for **Office‑style collaborative formats** (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx).  
  - Non‑collaborative files (e.g., .pdf, .jpg, .txt) are shared in **view‑only** mode.  
  - Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2382/share-data-from-the-kdrive-web-app  

- **Default behaviors**  
  - A newly created share link is **inactive** until you explicitly activate it.  
  - By default, shares provide **read‑only access**; editing must be enabled manually for supported formats.  
  - All shares are listed in the **“Shares”** menu of the kDrive web app, which automatically displays items shared with you, by you, and public links.  
  - Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2410/understanding-kdrive-folders-personal-shared-common  

- **Related actions**  
  - You can **modify** or **revoke** a share at any time.

**What a Drop Box is in kDrive**  
- A Drop Box is a special folder that lets you **collect files or folders from external contacts** without requiring them to have a kDrive account.  
- Files deposited in the Drop Box are **automatically stored in the kDrive folder you selected** and are treated as regular files in your storage.  
- You can control who can use the Drop Box, set notifications, add a password or expiration date, and limit the storage space that the Drop Box can use.  
- The feature is available on the **kDrive Web app** (online service <https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive>) and works whether the target location is a **personal folder (My Folder)** or a **shared/Organization Folder**.  
- *(Source: Manage kDrive drop boxes – Infomaniak documentation)*  
  <https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2386/manage-kdrive-drop-boxes>

**Prerequisites & Limitations**  
- You must have an active kDrive account and be **logged into the kDrive Web app**.  
- The Drop Box can only be created **inside a folder where you have write permission** (your personal “My Folder” or a shared folder you own/moderate).  
- Availability may depend on your **kDrive offer** – the documentation notes that “depending on the kDrive offer you have you can create (or multiple) drop boxes”.  
- Not all advanced options (e.g., password protection, expiration) are necessarily available on every plan; they are described as “advanced options” that can be set when creating the box.  
- *(Source: same FAQ page)*  
  <https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2386/manage-kdrive-drop-boxes>

**How to create a Drop Box – step‑by‑step**  

1. **Open the kDrive Web app**  
   - Go to <https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive>.  

2. **Navigate to the target folder**  
   - Use the left‑hand directory to reach the folder that will host the Drop Box:  
     - *Personal folder (My Folder)* → for private collections.  
     - *Shared folder (Organization Folders)* → if you want other kDrive users to see the deposited files.  

3. **Create a new Drop Box**  
   - Click the blue **New** button in that directory.  
   - From the New menu, select **Drop Box**.  

4. **Configure the Drop Box**  
   - **Enter a name** for the Drop Box.  
   - The full internal path to the containing folder is shown for reference.  
   - (Optional) Choose advanced settings such as:  
     - Receive an email notification when a file is deposited.  
     - Protect the folder with a password.  
     - Set an expiration date for the Drop Box.  
     - Limit the storage space allocated to the Drop Box.  
   - Click the blue **Create** button to finish.  

5. **Share the Drop Box** (after creation)  
   - You can **share the Drop Box link** directly or click **Send by email** to invite contacts.  
   - Advanced options (notifications, password, expiration, storage limit) can be edited later via the **Settings** (⋮) menu.  

*(Source: Manage kDrive drop boxes – creation steps and sharing options)*  
<https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2386/manage-kdrive-drop-boxes>

**What you can do with a Drop Box after it’s created**  
- **Share the link** with anyone (including external guests) so they can upload files.  
- **Receive email notifications** whenever a new file is deposited (if you enabled this option).  
- **Protect the Drop Box** with a password or set an expiration date to limit its lifetime.  
- **Limit storage space** so the Drop Box cannot consume unlimited capacity.  
- **Disable or modify** the Drop Box later:  
  - Right‑click (or use the ⋮ menu) → **Disable** to turn it into a regular folder without deleting existing files, or **Settings** to change advanced options.  
  *(Source: Disable or modify a drop box)*  
  <https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2386/manage-kdrive-drop-boxes>

**Key notes & warnings**  
- The Drop Box **does not import shared content** from other services; it only receives files that are uploaded directly to it.

- *(Source: same FAQ page – sharing, advanced options, and disabling)*  
  <https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2386/manage-kdrive-drop-boxes>

---  

**In summary**: a Drop Box in kDrive is a dedicated folder for collecting files from external contacts, created directly in the kDrive Web app by navigating to the desired location, clicking **New → Drop Box**, naming it, (optionally) configuring advanced settings, and then sharing the link. It works within your existing kDrive storage limits and can be managed (share, password‑protect, set expiration, disable) at any time.

question: How do I resolve sync conflicts in kDrive?
ground_truth: Sync conflicts occur when: a file is modified locally AND on kDrive Web simultaneously, or during conflicting create/move operations. Resolution: kDrive Web version is kept, local version is saved as '[filename]_conflict'. Options: 1) Keep both (only original syncs). 2) Delete _conflict if it's older. 3) Delete original and rename _conflict to sync it. 4) Manually merge then delete _conflict. To view conflicts: click kDrive icon > info button > view events. From version 3.6.11, locally modified files are moved to 'kDrive Rescue Folder' instead of deleted. Avoid conflicts by not working on the same file with multiple people.
key_points: conflicts when same file modified locally and online
can keep both, delete, or merge
actual_response:
**Resolving synchronization conflicts in kDrive**

- **What automatically happens (prerequisites & default behavior)**
  - You need the kDrive desktop app installed and must have edit rights on the file.  
  - When a conflict occurs, kDrive keeps the Web version unchanged, saves your local version as `[filename]_conflict`, and the conflicting file is **not** synchronized with the cloud. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]  
  - The conflicted file appears with an exclamation mark and the note `conflicted copy` in its name.

- **Options for handling the conflict**
  - Keep both versions (only the original file will continue to sync).  
  - Delete the `_conflict` file if it is the older/least‑recent version.  
  - Delete the original version (not the `_conflict`) if it is obsolete, then rename the `_conflict` to synchronize it.  
  - Manually merge the two versions before deleting the `_conflict`. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]

- **Step‑by‑step manual resolution (when automatic resolution fails)**
  1. Open both the original file and the conflicted copy.  
  2. Compare the differences.  
  3. Retrieve the needed information from the conflict file (the one with the exclamation mark) into the base file.  
  4. Delete the conflict file that is **not** synchronized (the one showing the exclamation mark and `conflicted copy`). [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]

- **Viewing and resolving conflicts via the kDrive app**
  1. Click the kDrive icon in the notification area (top‑right on macOS, bottom‑right on Windows, double‑click on Linux taskbar).  
  2. Click the information button at the top.  
  3. Click the listed event to view details.  
  4. Conflicts appear in a dedicated **“Conflicts”** tab where you can choose to:  
     - Send the local version to the server (i.e., synchronize it), or  
     - Move the local version to the recycle bin. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]

- **Recommendations to avoid conflicts**
  - Do not work on the same file with multiple people, except for Word, Excel, or PowerPoint documents that are edited online.  
  - Synchronize your offline modifications before making the same file the subject of online edits.  
  - Avoid creating folders that have the same name as folders you do not synchronize on a device. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]

- **Version‑specific and special‑case behavior**
  - **Pre‑3.6.11**: the kDrive Web version is always prioritized; the local version is renamed with “`_conflict`”. Deletions on the Web side usually keep the local file for resynchronization; move cycles are cancelled and recomputed based on the Web state. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]
  - **From version 3.6.11 onward**:  
    - “Placeholder” files (dehydrated via Lite Sync) are automatically deleted locally; if they still exist on kDrive Web they are correctly resynchronized.  
    - Regular files: the kDrive Web version remains prioritized; conflicting locals are renamed “`_conflict`”.  
    - **Exception**: if a locally modified file would be deleted according to the Web state, it is moved to a folder named **kDrive Rescue Folder** instead of being deleted, protecting your changes. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]  
  - **Parent folder deletion**: locally modified files are preserved.  
  - **Move cycles** are resolved in favor of the kDrive Web state.  
  - **Rename conflicts** prioritize the kDrive Web version. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]

- **Lite Sync considerations (platform limitation & technical spec)**
  - Placeholder files are “dehydrated”; they are automatically removed locally during a conflict, but if they still exist on the Web they sync back correctly. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]  
  - When disabling Lite Sync, ensure enough free disk space; otherwise synchronization will be paused until you select files to sync. [[2](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2562/manage-the-lite-sync-kdrive-option-windows)]

- **Re‑installation / configuration‑retention warning**
  - Uninstalling and reinstalling kDrive without deleting the configuration can create conflicts if changes were made on kDrive Web while the app was gone.  
  - To prevent this, either **do not keep the configuration** during uninstallation or **fully synchronize** all data before uninstalling. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]

- **Important warnings / notes**
  - Conflict files are **not** synchronized; they remain only on the device where they were created. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]  
  - Do not delete the wrong version; keep the most recent or required file.  
  - If you do not see conflict files on all devices, this is normal – the conflict file is not synced and only the author of the changes should resolve it. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]  
  - If the kDrive desktop app icon is green but you still encounter problems, consult the dedicated troubleshooting guide. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]  
  - Files that would be deleted are moved to a **kDrive Rescue Folder** as a safety net. [[1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict)]

- **Related actions you might also need**
  - Force kDrive to synchronize hidden and excluded files. [[3](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2504)]  
  - Restore a kDrive file to a previous version. [[3](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2384)]  
  - Restore a deleted kDrive file. [[3](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2383)]  
  - Clear the mobile app kDrive cache. [[3](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1561)]  
  - Clear the browser cache. [[3](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/793)]

question: How do I manage user rights in kDrive?
ground_truth: kDrive has 2 permission levels: 1) Administrator - same rights as owner (sharing, statistics, restore/delete folders, import data, access all files). 2) User - access folders at root, create/share content, but cannot manage product, view statistics, or create root folders. To modify: 1) Go to ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive. 2) Click action menu next to the kDrive. 3) Click 'Manage users'. 4) Select user and choose access level. Note: Don't confuse Manager rights (product management) with kDrive rights (data access). A user can have restricted Manager rights but be Administrator in kDrive.
key_points: don't confuse Manager rights with kDrive rights
actual_response:
**Managing user rights in kDrive – step‑by‑step**

Below is a complete walk‑through extracted from the official Infomaniak documentation. Every step includes the necessary prerequisites, role requirements, technical options, warnings and related actions. All sources are cited with their URLs.

---  

### 1️⃣ Prerequisites you must meet  
- You need an **Infomaniak account** and be part of an **Organization** (you are automatically the legal representative if you created the Organization) [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1610/manage-a-organization-users-product-access]  
- Your Organization must have a **kDrive offer with enough available user quotas** [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2364/manage-kdrive-users]  
- To **modify rights** you must have the **Organization‑administrator** (or a role that allows product‑access management) [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1610/manage-a-organization-users-product-access]  

### 2️⃣ Open the kDrive Web interface  
1. Go to the kDrive web app: **https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive** [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights]  
2. In the left‑hand sidebar **select the kDrive** you want to manage from the dropdown menu [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights]  

### 3️⃣ Access the *Manage users* panel  
3. Click the **action menu (⋮)** located to the right of the selected kDrive item [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights]  
4. Choose **“Manage users”** from the menu [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights]  

### 4️⃣ Set the desired permission level  
5. In the *Manage users* window you can:  
   - **Add a new user** (they must first accept the invitation with their own Infomaniak account) [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2364/manage-kdrive-users]  
   - **Edit an existing user’s rights** – you can switch between two main roles:  

     | Role | What the user can do | What they **cannot** do |
     |------|----------------------|--------------------------|
     | **Administrator** | Same rights as the kDrive owner: share files/folders, view + manage statistics, activity reports, restore/delete folders, import external data, access the dashboard, etc. | – |
     | **User** | Access root folders, view/modify shared content, create/share their own files/folders, manage personal directory | Cannot access **administrative management** of kDrive (no user‑management, no statistics, no creation/deletion of root folders, no imports, no dashboard) [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights] |
   - **Technical and/or Statistical rights** can be toggled separately:  
     - *Technical only* → user sees only storage information.  
     - *Statistics only* → user sees the dashboard but not technical details.  
     - *Both disabled* → user can see only basic storage info. [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights]  

6. After choosing the role, **save the changes**.  

### 5️⃣ Advanced actions you can perform on a user  
- **Block access** or **completely remove** a user from the kDrive via the same action menu (⋮) next to the user [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights]  
- **Replace a kDrive Solo administrator** if needed (useful when re‑assigning ownership) – involves selecting *Dashboard → Manage users → Replace user* and deciding whether to keep or delete existing data [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2364/manage-kdrive-users]  

### 6️⃣ Important warnings / notes  
- **Modification may fail** if the user still holds an **Administrator role at the Organization level**. In that case you must first **downgrade their Organization role to “User”** before the kDrive permission change becomes available [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights]  
- **Guests** (external users) have **limited permissions**; they cannot manage categories, view statistics, or create root folders [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights]  
- **Organization Folders** are common to all users, but sharing inside them can be restricted by the administrator [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights]  
- When a user only has **User** rights, they **cannot create a new folder at the root of “Organization Folders”**; an **Administrator** role is required for that action [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights]  
- Public sharing links are indicated by a **green icon** in the “*Who has access*” column [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2501/understanding-kdrive-permissions]  

### 7️⃣ Related actions you might need later  
- **Manage folder/category permissions** to further classify data [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2628]  
- **Convert a user from Administrator to User** (or vice‑versa) by repeating steps 3‑5.  
- **Block or delete a user** if they no longer need access [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights]  
- **Synchronize notes or devices** (e.g., Joplin, Qnap, Synology) – see the “Go further with kDrive” section for integration guides [Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2366/getting-started-guide-kdrive]  

---  

#### Quick reference checklist  

- ✅ Verify you are an **Organization admin** and have a **kDrive plan with free user slots**.  
- ✅ Open **ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive** → select kDrive → **(⋮) → Manage users**.  
- ✅ Choose **Administrator** or **User** role; optionally enable **Technical** and/or **Statistical** rights.  
- ✅ Save → test the permissions (e.g., try creating a root folder; only Administrators can).  
- ⚠️ If changes are blocked, **downgrade the user’s Organization role** first.  
- 📌 Remember: **Guests** have restricted rights; **public links** appear with a green icon.

question: How do I sync kDrive with my Synology NAS?
ground_truth: To sync kDrive with Synology NAS via WebDAV: Prerequisites: Synology NAS accessible from Internet, know your kDrive ID. Steps: 1) Log in to Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM). 2) Install Cloud Sync from Package Center if needed. 3) Open Cloud Sync. 4) Click + to add a Cloud. 5) Choose WebDAV. 6) Enter: Server address: https://[kDriveID].connect.kdrive.infomaniak.com, Username: Infomaniak email, Password: create an application password. 7) Select local folder, destination, and sync type: Bidirectional (changes in both directions), Download remote only (backup kDrive to NAS), or Download local only (backup NAS to kDrive).
key_points: Bidirectional, Download remote, or Download local sync
actual_response:
- **Prerequisites**  
  - You must have a Synology NAS that is reachable from the Internet (e.g., via DDNS or port‑forwarding).  
  - You must know your **kDrive identifier (kDrive ID)** – see the dedicated FAQ for details: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2409  

- **Installation & setup**  
  1. Log in to your Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM).  
  2. If the **Cloud Sync** application is not yet installed, download and install it from the Synology **Package Center**.  
  3. Open **Cloud Sync**.  
  4. Click the **+** button at the bottom‑left to add a new cloud location.  
  5. Choose **WebDAV** from the list of available cloud types.  
  6. Enter the account parameters:  
     - **Server address:** `https://<YOUR_kDRIVE_ID>.connect.kdrive.infomaniak.com` (replace `<YOUR_kDRIVE_ID>` with your actual kDrive identifier)  
     - **Username:** your Infomaniak email address  
     - **Password:** an **application password** created specifically for this WebDAV connection  
  7. Select the **local folder** on your Synology that you want to use as the source and the **destination folder** on the NAS (or vice‑versa).  
  8. Choose the synchronization direction:  
     - **Bidirectional** – changes made will be reflected in both directions.  
     - **Download only remote changes** – ideal for saving a kDrive folder to your NAS.  
     - **Download only local changes** – ideal for saving data from your NAS to a kDrive.  
  9. Save the configuration and start the sync.  

- **Additional notes**  
  - This method uses the **WebDAV** protocol via Synology’s **Cloud Sync** app; it is the recommended way to integrate kDrive with a Synology NAS.  
  - You can later modify or remove the WebDAV connection from Cloud Sync if you no longer wish to sync.  
  - Ensure the server address and application password are correctly entered; otherwise the connection will fail.  

**Source:** https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2404/sync-synology-with-kdrive

question: How do I create a channel in kChat?
ground_truth: To create a channel in kChat: 1) Click the button in the left sidebar of kChat web app (ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat). 2) Click 'Create a new channel'. 3) Set: A) Name (modifiable later), B) URL (lowercase, numbers, dots, dashes, underscores), C) Private or Public status, D) Description. Every Organization has a default 'General' channel for all users. Public channels are visible to all; Private channels require invitation. To convert public to private: click channel > chevron > Convert (permanent). To leave: chevron > Leave. To archive: chevron > Archive. Can also add to favorites, mute, or organize by categories.
actual_response:
**How to create a new channel in kChat**

**Prerequisites**  
- You must be a member of an Organization that uses a kSuite plan (the number of private channels you can create is limited by the plan you have purchased) – see the quota limits on the sales page.  
- Access to the kChat web app (**ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat**) or the desktop client (macOS / Windows / Linux). No specific admin role is required to create a channel, but you need to be logged in to an active Organization.  
- The channel will be subject to the general kChat limits on private/public channels (see “Private channels … are limited in number according to the kSuite offer acquired”).  
(Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2732/manage-a-kchat-channel)

**Platform limitations**  
- Channel creation is only available through the **kChat web interface** or the **desktop client**; it is not performed via mobile apps.  
- All channel‑related settings (name, URL, private/public status) can be edited later.  

**Technical specifications**  
- **Name**: Any text; can be modified after creation.  
- **URL slug**: By default it mirrors the channel name, but you may edit it using only **lowercase letters, numbers, dots (.), dashes (‑), and underscores (_)** – these characters can also be changed later.  
- **Type**: Choose **PRIVATE** or **PUBLIC** at creation; the status can be switched later.  
- **Default behavior**: Every Organization automatically includes a **General Channel** where all users are added automatically; you can create additional channels on top of this default one.  

**Step‑by‑step creation**  

- **Step 1** – Open kChat: launch the web app at **ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat** or start the desktop application.  
- **Step 2** – In the **left sidebar**, click the button that opens the channel creation menu (the “Create a new channel” button).  
- **Step 3** – Click **Create a new channel**.  
- **Step 4** – Enter a **name** for the channel (this can be changed later).  
- **Step 5** – (Optional) Edit the **URL slug** if you want a custom address; remember it must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, “.”, “‑”, or “_”.  
- **Step 6** – Select the **PRIVATE** or **PUBLIC** status for the channel (this can be changed later).  
- **Step 7** – Confirm the creation. The new channel will appear in the left sidebar and is now ready for discussions, file exchanges, and video conferences.  

(Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2732/manage-a-kchat-channel)

**Important warnings / notes**  
- **Quota limit**: Private (and public/guest) channels are limited in number according to your kSuite plan; creating more channels than your plan allows will block further creations.  
- **Archiving vs. deleting**:  
  - *Archive* a channel if you want to keep it but stop new messages; archived channels no longer count toward your quota and can be unarchived later.  
  - *Delete* a channel permanently removes all its data; this action cannot be undone.  
- **Leaving a channel**:  
  - If you leave a **private** channel, it disappears from search results unless you have its URL or are reinvited.  
  - If you leave a **public** channel, you can still re‑join it later via search even if it has been archived.  
(Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2732/manage-a-kchat-channel)

**Related actions you can perform after creation**  
- **Add to Favorites** – click the star icon at the top of the channel to keep it in a dedicated Favorites section (user‑specific).  
- **Mute** – use the ⋮ menu to silence notifications for a channel.  
- **Organize by categories** – create categories via the **+** button in the sidebar and drag the channel into them for personal organization.  
- **Invite or manage members** – click the participant icon below the channel title to view, invite, remove, or promote members (requires sufficient permissions).  
- **Archive / leave / delete** – manage the channel’s lifecycle as described above.  
- **Start conversations** – exchange messages, share files, and start video meetings (kMeet) directly from the channel.  

**How to use the newly created channel**  
- Begin typing messages in the composition field to start a conversation.  
- Use slash commands (`/`) for quick actions (e.g., `/call` to start a video call).  
- Share documents, images, or other files by dragging them into the chat window.  
- Schedule a kMeet video conference by clicking the **Call** button in the channel’s conversation area.  

All of the above steps and details are taken from the official Infomaniak documentation on managing kChat channels. (Source: https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2732/manage-a-kchat-channel)

question: What slash commands are available in kChat?
ground_truth: To use slash commands in kChat: 1) Click in the composition field. 2) Type / followed by the command. 3) Send. Typing just / shows available commands in a modal (like going offline). You can create custom slash commands: 1) Open kChat web or desktop app. 2) Click 'New' icon next to organization name. 3) Click 'Integrations'. 4) Click 'Slash command'. 5) Add a command with name, trigger, content type, and action. Custom commands can call external APIs or run scripts. Note: External users cannot see the Integrations menu.
actual_response:
**Available slash commands in kChat**

- **How to open the command list**  
  - Click in the composition field of a channel, type `/` and a modal appears showing all commands you can execute. This modal includes built‑in commands such as “going offline” as an example. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands))

- **Built‑in slash commands**  
  - The documentation only explicitly mentions that the modal contains commands like “going offline”. The full table of main commands is referenced but not reproduced in the excerpt. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands))

- **Creating or editing custom slash commands**  
  - **Prerequisites** – You must be an internal user (not an external guest) to see the *Integrations* menu where custom commands are added. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands))  
  - **Platform limitation** – Custom commands can only be added via the Web kChat app or the desktop app; external users do not have access to this menu. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands))  
  - **Steps** –  
    1. Open kChat (Web or desktop).  
    2. Click **New** next to your organization name → **Integrations** → **Slash command**.  
    3. Click **Add a command** and configure: name, trigger (without the `/`), expected content type, action to execute, optional UI elements (dropdowns, checkboxes), etc.  
    4. Save the command and test it to ensure it works. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands))

- **User role requirements**  
  - Only users with sufficient permissions (internal members) can create, edit, or manage slash commands. External guests cannot access the *Integrations* menu and are limited to the built‑in commands that are already available. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands))  
  - Guests can use slash commands but cannot perform privileged actions such as inviting members, renaming channels, or modifying headers via slash commands. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat))

- **Technical specifications / usage**  
  - A slash command is invoked by typing `/` followed by the command name (without the leading slash) in the channel’s message box and confirming.  
  - The command can be set to expect a specific content type and to execute an action such as calling an external API, running a script, or displaying a predefined response. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands))

- **Important warnings / notes**  
  - Creating custom slash commands may require programming skills; you must follow security best practices to avoid vulnerabilities. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands))  
  - Guests have limited permissions – they can use slash commands but cannot execute restricted commands (e.g., inviting members, renaming channels). ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat))

- **Default behavior**  
  - Typing only `/` automatically opens the command modal that lists all available slash commands, including built‑in ones like “going offline”. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands))  
  - New channels are automatically added to the General channel by default. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2734/customize-kchat))

- **Related actions**  
  - After saving a custom command you can **test** it to verify functionality.  
  - Commands can be **disabled**, **edited**, or **removed** via the same *Integrations → Slash command* interface.  
  - The command list can always be re‑opened by typing `/` in any channel. ([Source](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands))

question: How can I connect external applications to kChat?
ground_truth: To connect external apps to kChat using webhooks: 1) Open kChat web or desktop app. 2) Click 'New' icon next to organization name. 3) Click 'Integrations'. 4) Access webhook categories. For incoming webhooks (receive messages from external apps): 1) Click 'Incoming Webhooks'. 2) Add name and description. 3) Select destination channel. 4) Save to get URL. 5) External app sends POST request with JSON: {"text": "message"}. For outgoing webhooks: kChat sends info when events occur. Parameters include channel override, username, icon_url. Response includes message details. Add ?slack_return_format=true for Slack-style response.

Outgoing webhooks send to external apps
POST request with JSON text field

**Connecting external applications to kChat – summary of the official guide**  

**Prerequisites**  
- You must **not be an external user** – external users do not see the *Integrations* menu, so only internal (registered) users can create/modify webhooks.  
- You need to access the kChat web or desktop application (online service <https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat> or the native macOS/Windows/Linux client).

**Platform / access**  
- Use the **kChat Web app** (ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat) **or** the **kChat desktop app** to manage integrations.

**Steps to set up an integration (incoming webhook)**  

1. **Open the Integrations menu**  
   - In the left‑hand sidebar of kChat, click the **New** icon next to your organization name, then select **Integrations**.  

2. **Choose a category**  
   - Pick the category that matches the type of integration you need (e.g., **Incoming Webhooks**).  

3. **Create a new webhook**  
   - Click the blue **Add incoming webhooks** button.  

4. **Configure the webhook**  
   - **Name** the webhook (any label you prefer).  
   - Add a **description** (max 500 characters).  
   - **Select the channel** that will receive the messages triggered by the webhook.  

5. **Save**  
   - After saving, kChat generates a **webhook URL** (e.g., `https://your-server-kchat.xyz/hooks/xxx-key-generated-xxx`).  
   - **Keep this URL confidential** – it must not be disclosed publicly.  

6. **Use the URL from your external app**  
   - Configure the external application to send HTTP POST requests to the obtained URL whenever you want to push a message or event into the selected kChat channel.  

**Technical notes**  
- The integration works via **webhooks only**; there is no native “import discussion history” from other platforms (Slack, Teams, Jabber, etc.).  
- Only **incoming webhooks** are described in the guide, but the concept of **outgoing webhooks** (kChat notifying external apps of events) is also mentioned in the preamble.  
- The generated URL follows the pattern shown above; no size limits or specific request formats are defined in the documentation.  

**Important caveats**  
- External users cannot access the *Integrations* menu, so they cannot create or edit webhooks themselves.  
- The quota for external users remains at **0 / 100** until the user completes registration; this does not affect webhook configuration but is relevant when inviting external participants.  
- The webhook URL must be kept secret; if it leaks, any external application could post to your channel.  

**Reference**  
- Official documentation: *“Connect external applications to kChat”* – <https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2001/connect-external-applications-to-kchat>  

---  

You can now connect any external application to kChat by creating an incoming webhook as outlined above and having the external app post to the generated URL. If you need more advanced integration options or run into permission issues, consider contacting Infomaniak support.

question: How do I translate a message in kChat?

**How to translate a message in kChat**

  2. Click on the **action menu (•••)** situated at the top‑right corner of that message.

question: How can I invite external users to kChat?
ground_truth: To invite external users to kChat: Prerequisites: Be Organization administrator with full kChat rights. Steps: 1) Access kChat at ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat or desktop app. 2) Click 'Invite members' button. 3) Click link to invite new user. 4) Enter email address(es). 5) Specify channel(s) they'll access. 6) Click send invitation. Invited users receive email with link to the channel. They must create Infomaniak account if needed. External users are not counted as regular users. Guests CAN: pin messages, use slash commands, add favorites, mute, update profile. Guests CANNOT: discover public channels, join open teams, create DMs with non-channel members, invite people.
key_points: external users not counted as users
actual_response:
**Prerequisites**  
- You must be an **Organization administrator with full rights granted for kChat** in order to invite external users [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
- The external user must be reachable by **email** (the address you will invite).  
- If the external user does not already have an Infomaniak account, they will need to **create one** during the invitation flow [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).

**How to send the invitation**  
- **Access kChat** via the **Web app** (https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat) **or** the **desktop application** (available on macOS, Windows, Linux) [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
- Click the **“Invite members”** button.  
- Click the **link to invite a new user**.  
- **Enter the email address(es)** of the person(s) you want to invite [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
- **Select the channel(s)** that the invited user will have access to [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
- Click the **blue “Send invitation”** button [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
- The invited person receives an **email with a link** that leads to the kChat interface and the channel you specified [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
- If the user does **not yet have an Infomaniak account**, they must **register**; during this pending phase they appear in the channel but are **not counted toward your external‑user quota** (the quota stays at **0/100** until registration completes) [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
- After successful registration, the user can **fully access kChat** and will be shown on your **my kSuite dashboard** as an external user [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).

**Platform limitations**  
- The invitation and member‑management actions are available **only via the Web app or the desktop client**; the documentation does not mention mobile‑app support [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).

**Permissions of invited external users (guests)**  
- **Can:**  
  - Pin messages to channels [2](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
  - Use most **slash commands** (except restricted ones) [2](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
  - Add the channel to **Favorites** [2](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
  - **Mute** a channel [2](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
  - Update their profile [2](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
  - Use **authentication methods** different from those of regular users [2](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
  - Open the kChat app (Web, mobile, or desktop) even if they are not yet a member of any other channel [2](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  

- **Cannot:**  
  - Discover **public channels**.  
  - Join **open teams**.  
  - Create **direct messages** or **group messages** with members who are not part of the same invited channel.  
  - **Invite other people** to any channel [2](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).

**Important warnings / notes**  
- External users are **restricted and external**; they are **not counted as regular kSuite users** until they finish registration [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
- There is a **quota limit of 0/100 external users**; pending invitations do **not** consume this quota, but once the user is active they will count toward the limit [1](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  
- Invitations remain **pending** until the external user completes registration; if they never register, you must **resend** the invitation.  
- External users **cannot discover public channels** or **join open teams**, so they can only interact within the channels you explicitly invite them to [2](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).  

**Managing invited members**  
- After an invitation is accepted, you can **view participants** by clicking the **character icon** next to the channel title [3](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1886/manage-kchat-members).  
- Use the **blue “Add” button** to invite more users or the **“Manage” button** to **remove a member** or **promote them to Administrator** of the channel [3](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1886/manage-kchat-members).  
- For broader member‑management tasks (e.g., auto‑membership of channels), refer to the guide on **managing kChat members** [3](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1886/manage-kchat-members).  

**Related actions**  
- You can **convert** an external user to a full kSuite user, **leave** the channel, or **archive** the channel if needed [3](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1886/manage-kchat-members).  
- Invitations can be **resent** or **revoked** through the same “Invite members” interface.  

**Sources**  
- [Invite an external user to use kChat](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat)  
- [Manage kChat members](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1886/manage-kchat-members)

question: What is Euria and how do I use it in kChat?
ground_truth: Euria is the AI assistant available in kSuite/kChat. It can perform calculations, translations, provide information, and answer questions. To use: 1) In kChat left sidebar, use channel search (bots appear as channels) or click + next to Direct Messages. 2) Search for 'bot' or the bot name. 3) Add the bot with [bot] tag. 4) Create a private discussion with the bot (not a group conversation). 5) Write to it like chatting with a person. New users automatically receive a welcome message from Euria. For AI summaries of discussions, refer to the separate summary feature guide.
key_points: Euria is AI assistant in kSuite

actual_response:
**What is Euria?**  
- Euria is Infomaniak’s AI conversational agent that can answer questions, perform calculations, translate texts, provide information, and summarize discussions within kChat. (https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2840/use-euria-on-kchat-conversational-agent)

**Prerequisites**  
- You must have an active kChat account within your organization. (https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2840/use-euria-on-kchat-conversational-agent)  
- No special user role is required; any regular user can add and interact with Euria bots. (https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2840/use-euria-on-kchat-conversational-agent)

**Platform limitations**  
- Group conversations with bots are not supported; you must create a private discussion channel with each bot individually. (https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2840/use-euria-on-kchat-conversational-agent)  
- Bots appear as channels in the left sidebar and can be added via the channel search or the “+” icon next to Direct Messages. (https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2840/use-euria-on-kchat-conversational-agent)

**Technical specifications**  
- Interaction is purely text‑based; Euria can handle calculations, translations, and generate AI‑generated summaries of discussion threads. (https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2840/use-euria-on-kchat-conversational-agent; https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2480/use-euria-on-kchat-summarize-a-discussion)

**User role requirements**  
- Any standard user can add Euria bots and start a conversation; no admin or moderator rights are needed. (https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2840/use-euria-on-kchat-conversational-agent)

**Important warnings / notes**
